title: An affine cover whose overlaps are separating pairs gives a separated scheme
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and (U_a) an open cover by affine opens [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose every U_a ∩ U_b is affine and its ring of sections is generated as a subring by the images of the two restriction maps from the section rings of U_a and U_b. (This is IsSeparatingPair X U_a U_b in the source library, with section rings on open subschemes identified by topIso.) Then X is a separated scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism], meaning X→Spec ℤ has closed-immersion diagonal [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Schemes Tag 01KP (2) for the absolute base Spec ℤ; proved source declaration Scheme.isSeparated_of_isSeparatingPair in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Separated

proof.text: For each pair U,V the product U×V over Spec ℤ is affine and the overlap U∩V is affine. The ring of sections of U×V is the pushout of the two section rings over ℤ, and so is generated as a ring by the two projection images. The map of rings induced by the overlap morphism U∩V→U×V takes those images to the two restriction images. Since these generate the overlap ring by hypothesis, its image is the whole overlap ring. Hence that ring map is surjective, and the overlap morphism is a closed immersion by the affine closed-immersion criterion. This is the proved source lemma isSeparatingPair_iff.

The products U_a×U_b cover X×X: choose cover opens containing each projection of a point. They are open subschemes and the preimage of U_a×U_b under the diagonal is U_a∩U_b, with the restriction of the diagonal identified with the overlap morphism of the first step. Closed immersion is local on the target, so the diagonal is a closed immersion. Thus X is separated. These steps are implemented by Scheme.isSeparated_of_isSeparatingPair using AffineTargetMorphismProperty.diagonal_of_openCover_source.
